Subject: Initial MSA redline: indemnity & escrow triggers

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Procurement at Ascent Bio ran the MSA/Order Form by our legal team and they pushed back on the indemnity sections. Key asks:

- We need clearer allocation for third-party IP claims (who defends, who pays).
- If Redwood insists on a full ‘right to defend’, Ascent wants an escrow-triggered remediation path if damages exceed a material threshold.
- Insurance offset mechanics: customer expects Redwood to use its insurance first and any residual to be covered as discussed.

I attached a redline with our position (Ascent_MSA_redline_v1.docx). High level proposal from our side: customer controls settlement for amounts below $500k; for larger claims, escrow kicks in and Redwood pays remediation costs up to the liability cap. We flagged AI-output attribution scenarios as well (we call these out in §6.2).

Can your team review and propose a compromise? Procurement would like a short list of concrete options we can take to our GC.

Thanks,
Aisha Kapoor
Sr. Procurement Manager | Ascent Bio

Aisha / David — I reviewed the redline and sketched three pragmatic pathways with pros/cons. I’m summarizing so Procurement can take discrete options to GC: 

1) Full Right to Defend (Redwood controls defense and settlement) + Escrow backstop (funded on trigger):
   - Pros: Preserves Redwood’s ability to manage litigation strategy and mitigate indemnity exposure.
   - Cons: Ascent loses settlement control; requires clearly defined escrow triggers and proof thresholds. Escrow funded on trigger (preferred for our cash flow).

2) Defense with Customer Consent for Settlements under $500k; Redwood defends above $500k and retains control + insurance offset language:
   - Pros: Compromise that gives Ascent voice on small settlements; limits Redwood’s exposure to large claims where we keep control.
   - Cons: Needs crisp approval process and timeline to avoid settlement stalemates. We’ll seek to cap customer’s unilateral settlement rights to trivial/defensive matters only.

3) Reimburse-only (Redwood pays amounts allocated by a neutral expert or court) + escrow as a liquidation mechanism:
   - Pros: Lower operational burden for Redwood.
   - Cons: Harder to accept commercially; increases negotiation friction and likely pricing impact.

Key clarifying questions for Ascent:
- Is the $500k number intended per-claim or aggregate over the term?
- Is escrow intended to be a separately held fund (third-party custodian) or an insurance-backed hold?
- For AI-output scenarios, does Ascent expect attribution analysis and evidence collection to be part of the notice? We can propose a short evidence-capture template (attached).

Suggested next step: I’m attaching an evidence_catalog_template.xlsx that defines minimum proof (claim notice, sample outputs, timestamps, ingestion logs, model/version). If Ascent agrees to pathway (2) we can draft specific settlement approval language: customer may not settle without Redwood consent for claims above $X, and for amounts below $500k customer may settle but Redwood may elect to step in within 10 business days.

I’ll draft redline language for options (1) and (2) and share by EOD tomorrow.

-Kim
Deputy GC, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: evidence_catalog_template.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB))

Aisha — appreciate the clear ask and Kimberly’s helpful breakdown. Quick commercial compromise that has worked for similar accounts:

- Use pathway (2) as a starting point. Insert explicit settlement approval mechanics: Ascent can propose settlements below $250k unilaterally; for amounts between $250k and $500k Ascent may propose but Redwood has 10 business days to elect to take control; above $500k Redwood will control defense and settlement decisions.
- Escrow: fund on trigger (not upfront). Trigger = final judgment or certified settlement > $500k or a binding appointment of remediation obligations by a court/arbitrator.
- Insurance offset: Redwood’s commercial general liability and E&O apply first; escrow covers remediation gaps up to the Order Form cap.

If that sounds acceptable, Kimberly and Marissa will prepare a clean and a redlined version (two-choice language) for Ascent’s GC to review. DocuSign-ready draft & HubSpot deal will be posted here: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/4831.

Can we lock a 30-min call tomorrow to run GC through the compromise and finalize the threshold numbers? Proposed times: 10:00–10:30am PT or 2:00–2:30pm PT.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
